To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HPV16 E6 and E7 oncoproteins induce a strong immune response in the cervical mucosa.

the human immune system can be activated to recognize, attack, and kill cervical cancer cells, that this immune response is associated with the regression of cervical cancer, and that the immune response is associated in part with the presence of HPV E6/E7-specific CD8+ T cells.
The host immune response to HPV infection and cervical cancer is characterized by the presence of both pro- and anti-inflammatory immune responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the host response to cervical cancer and the role of the host immune response in determining the outcome of cervical cancer.
the host immune responses to cervical neoplasia, with a focus on the immune cells present in the tumor microenvironment and the cytokines produced by these cells.
understanding the role of the host immune response in the pathogenesis and treatment of cervical cancer and its precursor lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of host immune responses in the pathogenesis and progression of cervical cancer is not well understood, although there are some indications that the host immune system may be involved.
the host immune system does respond to cervical cancer.
there is no evidence of a protective role of the host immune response against cervical cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the host response to cervical cancer is a complex interaction of immune cells and cytokines that are involved in the development, progression and treatment of this cancer.
the host immune response to cervical cancer is a complex process, with the balance of immune responses tipping towards a pro-tumour environment.
HPV is a necessary but not sufficient cause for cervical cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the human papillomavirus (HPV) E7 oncoprotein, which is expressed by all cervical cancers, is a potent immunogenic antigen that elicits strong immune responses in patients with cervical cancer and in animal models.
the host immune system can play a role in the pathogenesis of cervical cancer.
the host immune response to cervical cancer is a complicated interplay between host and tumor.
